limits.counts: Research Articles: a main text of at most 3,000 words, plus an abstract, 3 to 5 display items (figures or tables) with brief legends, about 50 main-text references and a structured acknowledgments section. Materials and Methods go in the supplementary materials. An extended format online: 'the main text can be up to 6000 words, with as many as 6 display items ... and up to 100 main-text references', justified in the cover letter. (https://www.science.org/content/page/science-information-authors (read in a browser 2026-11-16))
limits.notes: science.org's instructions for an initial manuscript and for a revised one (read in a browser 2026-11-16; the initial page's Internet Archive copy of 2025-08-10 says the same): 'Titles should be no more than 96 characters (including spaces)'; 'The abstract should be 125 words or less', with no citations or abbreviations; figure captions start with a bold short title and no caption is over 200 words. Parts, in order: Title, Authors, Affiliations, Abstract, Main Text, References and Notes, Acknowledgments (with Funding, Author contributions, Diversity, equity, ethics, and inclusion [optional], Competing interests, and Data, code, and materials availability), List of Supplementary Materials, figure and table captions. Neither page asks for a one-sentence summary. Length limits: see counts (the information-for-authors page, read in a browser 2026-11-16).
